title: A copy of both streams reads the film once
description: JS-026's copy of both opens the source twice, as a video copy with re-encoded audio does: the second input exists only so a re-encoded AAC track can start early on its own grid. A copied track needs neither, so the second open only doubles what a worker reads: ten times the film's bitrate while the job runs and twice its bytes per full watch, which on S3 is twice the egress and on a NAS twice the load. JS-026's design reviewer measured that one input splices the same segments.
acceptanceCriteria: A job copying both the video and the audio opens the source once: ffmpeg has one input, and on S3 the worker's range proxy serves one stream of the film's bytes, measured in a test with real ffmpeg
Segments still splice after a restart on another worker exactly as JS-026's checks require (every film and restart point of TestCopyOfBothSplicesTheSameSegments)
Played and sought in jellyfin-web in CI's Chrome as JS-026's scenario does
docs/transcoding.md and DOMAINS 48 state the reading cost of a copy of both, and docs/status.md drops the note that it opens the file twice
notes: JS-026's design reviewer ran a scratch experiment: one input at the copy's flags gave identical fragments to two inputs for H.264 with AC3 and E-AC3 in Matroska (13 of 13) and for AAC in MP4 after the first fragment. The implementer did not take it because JS-026's locked e2e helper reads the audio map from the second input (-map 1:N); this task changes that helper. Priority 5, right after JS-026: copies are the common path for a remux library, and halving their reads helps the S3 and NAS costs every copy-both viewer incurs. Built 2026-11-09: CopyCommand maps a copied audio track from the one input (-map 0:N); a copy with re-encoded audio keeps its two inputs. TestACopyOfBothStreamsFromS3ReadsTheFilmOnce measures the bytes the range proxy serves on SeaweedFS and Garage: 2.00 times the film before, once after (QA put the old command back and saw it fail). Every splice case of JS-026 still passes, AAC in MP4 byte for byte, under ffmpeg 9.0.2 and 6.1.1; the transcode e2e gate passed 60 of 60. The first Verify round sent the task back only because one integration shard had not finished when the tier gate looked; it passed.
